title: 1951 AHSME Problem 14
statement: In connection with proof in geometry, indicate which one of the following statements is incorrect:

answerChoices.label: A
answerChoices.text: Some statements are accepted without being proved.

answerChoices.label: B
answerChoices.text:
In some instances there is more than one correct order in
proving certain propositions.

answerChoices.label: C
answerChoices.text:
Every term used in a proof must have been
defined previously.

answerChoices.label: D
answerChoices.text:
It is not possible to arrive by correct reasoning at a true
conclusion if, in the given, there is an untrue proposition.

answerChoices.label: E
answerChoices.text:
Indirect proof can be used whenever there are two or more
contrary propositions.

solutions.text:
An axiomatic development begins with primitive terms that are deliberately left undefined, as well as statements accepted without proof. Therefore it is not true that every term in a proof must previously have been defined.

Thus, the intended correct answer is C.
hints: Distinguish undefined primitive terms from unproved axioms
An axiomatic system cannot define every term without an infinite regress
